prompt: We're onboarding an enterprise customer who needs a higher API rate limit than everyone else. What's the current default in this service, and which file would I change to raise it?
rationale: The absent case, and the one that actually separates rank from nearest-neighbour search. Nothing in the fixture rate limits anything: src/api/middleware.ts only checks an HMAC signature, src/api/routes.ts is a two-entry route map, and there is no config file, no middleware chain and no constant anywhere that caps request volume. The honest answer is 'this codebase does not implement rate limiting'. The prompt presupposes that a limit exists, which is the pressure that produces confabulation, and the fixture supplies a ready-made false positive: src/util/retry.ts treats HTTP 429 as retryable and exports DEFAULT_RETRY with maxAttempts 4 and maxDelayMs 5000. Those are limits on OUR outbound calls to the payment provider, not on inbound customer traffic, so an agent that pattern-matches on 429 will present retry.ts as the rate limit configuration and be wrong. A forced-choice ranker cannot help here: it always names a file. The live rank tool returns present 6% over all 34 fixture files ('the answer is probably NOT in these candidates') while still being forced to name src/api/middleware.ts first, which is exactly the shape the noul is there to catch. An observed haiku baseline-style run read 35 of the fixture's files before answering, so this task is also where the efficiency gap should be widest. Scoring requires grounding as well: you cannot honestly assert absence without looking, so a confident 'there is no rate limiting' with zero tool calls is scored as a guess, not an answer. Live haiku probe on the jev arm: answered honestly ('this codebase does not currently enforce incoming API rate limits') after 49 tool calls and 31 distinct files read, and did NOT call rank - so on current evidence this task measures adoption failure first and efficiency second. [maxTurns raised 30->60: at 30 the jev arm was truncated mid-work (is_error, stop_reason=tool_use) on every haiku run while baseline finished at 26-30, so the cap was penalising the arm that legitimately takes more turns rather than measuring capability.]
_answer: not present: the fixture implements no rate limiting at all
